caption: The drawing depicts a detailed section of an architectural structure resembling a decorated wall and archway corner. The arch is outlined in blue and green with interior shading in blue tones and highlighted with red scalloped designs on the edge. Adjacent to the arch is a vertical column featuring a pinkish-red band bordered with thin black lines and cross-hatched for shading. The column has a central vertical decoration of symmetrical, lanceolate green leaves, and is topped by a textured gray stone capital. Horizontal geometric ornamentation in blue and yellow, composed of interlinked circular patterns, runs just below the capital and continues along the wall as a frieze. Below this frieze, the wall is divided into sections: a pale cream upper section, a lower deep pink section, and horizontal blue stripes marking the separation between colors. At the bottom left, part of the base shows unpainted brown stones, indicating exposed masonry. The background is plain and uncolored. The drawing is signed “R.W.G. Taylor 1936” in the lower right corner.
title: Grille Doors of Wood
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
